about.title: Hemet Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Seven people died in traffic collisions in Hemet in 2025, out of 273 injury crashes that hurt 419 others. Each of those numbers was someone's parent, partner, or child. When a death traces back to another person's carelessness — on Florida Avenue, along Sanderson Avenue, or elsewhere in the city — California law gives certain family members a way to seek accountability in civil court. A wrongful death claim is not a criminal case. Prosecutors decide whether to file charges; your family decides whether to pursue compensation for funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Standing is limited: a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Hemet families with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency.

items.question: My loved one was killed in a crash on Florida Avenue and the other driver is facing charges. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, the two proceed on separate tracks. The criminal case in Riverside County is brought by the District Attorney and focuses on punishment, not on your family's losses. A wrongful death claim is the civil action that addresses funeral expenses, lost support, and the loss of companionship, and it can move forward regardless of how the criminal case resolves.

items.question: What can our family actually recover in a California wrongful death case?
items.answer: Recoverable losses generally include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided over their lifetime, and the loss of their love, companionship, comfort, and guidance. The value depends on your specific circumstances, so no one can responsibly quote a figure in advance. An attorney will walk through what applies to your family.

items.question: How long do we have to act after a death in Hemet?
items.answer: In most cases, California allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity might be at fault — for example, a road maintained by the city or county — a separate claim must be presented much sooner, often within six months. Because those shorter deadlines are easy to miss during grief, it helps to speak with an attorney early even if you are not ready to decide.
